title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt (as-of 2026-12-31) — the series' most durable first vintage, on its only spotless release date, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by THIS event's own research session 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes). The 2027 table's March row reads '31' in the column headed 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt at end of previous quarter' — a separate dated column from the '18' cells in the Monthly and Quarterly-derivatives columns — under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time', and its note block states the rule: 'The release dates are the last business day of each quarter (March, June, September, and December).' Corroborated by a SECOND Treasury primary fetched the same session, home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system-home-page/tic-forms-instructions/us-gross-external-debt (HTTP 200, 174,128 bytes), which is more specific than the release-dates page and puts THIS release in the 4 PM group explicitly: 'Releases are made at 4 PM in Washington D.C. on the last business day of March, June, and September, and at 10 AM on the last business day of December.' PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-09 on the bar tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-06-30 and tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26 set (one named Treasury primary plus independent mechanical corroboration), with the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this is the event's own session re-fetching, not either of the two sweeps that proposed it. The mechanical corroboration is empirical and is STRONGER FOR MARCH THAN FOR ANY OTHER QUARTER: all 134 archived Table A vintages indexed by the statistics page were fetched from ticdata.treasury.gov this session and each one's own publication stamp read, giving 59 genuine first-vintage publications 2010-2026. The last-business-day rule reproduces 54 of the 59 at offset +0 — but split by edition, MARCH IS 15 OF 15 AT +0 WITH NO EXCEPTIONS, against September 14/14, June 13/15 and December 12/15. All five historical slips in the series are June or December releases (2019-01-31 at +31 during the 35-day funding lapse; 2026-01-16 at +16, flagged '16 (delayed)' on Treasury's own page; 2024-12-30 at -1; 2025-07-02 at +2; 2012-06-30 at +1). 2027-03-31 is a Wednesday and is March 2027's last business day, recomputed from 5 U.S.C. 6103 holiday rules rather than a list. CONFIRMED COVERS THE SCHEDULED DATE AND NOTHING ELSE: the release-dates page carries the standing notice 'When Federal Government offices in Washington D.C. are closed on a release date, that date will be revised after offices reopen'. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-09) after reading BOTH proposals that created it — `from-tic-monthly-2027-03-18` (filed as a taxonomy correction: the '31' sits in a separate dated column and is this release, not a third cut of the 03-18 monthly) and `from-tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-06-30` (filed as the June forecast's last checkpoint) — now shadowed. Neither proposer asked what a March edition IS, and it has a character of its own that is the opposite of the intuitive reading. WHAT THIS RELEASE PUBLISHES: the gross external debt position as-of 2026-12-31, on the series' standing one-quarter lag, with no accompanying press release (the release-dates page states this explicitly, and it is the ground on which tic-monthly-2027-02-18 first declined the event). IT REVISES NOTHING, and that is now a census rather than a convention: of the 75 non-first Table A vintages surviving in the archive, 75 carry a JUNE publication stamp — zero March, zero September, zero December, 2010 through 2026 — independently reproducing the sibling's finding on a re-fetched archive. WHAT IS NEW HERE: the March edition publishes the number this series revises LEAST. Grouping every first-vintage-to-latest-vintage revision by as-of quarter (n=58 pairs), the as-of-Q4 position the March edition publishes is restated by a mean 0.784% of level ($145.0bn, median 0.600%, n=15), tied-lowest with as-of-Q1 (0.792%), against 1.901% ($376.4bn) for as-of-Q2 and 1.265% for as-of-Q3; Q4 vs the other three is t=-1.75, p=0.080. And it earns that while waiting only 91 days for its restatement, the shortest wait in the series — shelf life and durability are not the same thing. THE REVISION CONCENTRATION IS ON END-JUNE, AND THE SURVEY IS STILL NOT THE MECHANISM: as-of-Q2 is the significant outlier (t=+2.15, p=0.031; p=0.008 excluding the 2024Q3 data event) and the only quarter with a negative mean signed revision (-1.088%), and end-June is exactly the Survey of Foreign Holdings of U.S. Securities' benchmark date — but on the sibling's own discriminator, Table A's market-valued 'Debt Securities: By Sector' memorandum across 45 BPM6 vintage pairs, as-of-Q2 has the SMALLEST |revision| of the four quarters ($35.4bn, 0.08 of |headline revision|) against $358.0bn for Q4 and $368.2bn for Q3, t=-1.51 p=0.132. Wrong sign for a survey story; the concentration is a banking / direct-investment phenomenon. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds — 16:00 ET publication after the equity cash close, data a quarter stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed, no press release — and on this event's own matched-control test: next-session |delta-10Y| after a March edition is 5.00bp (n=15) against 4.73bp after the other three quarterly editions (p=0.78), and against all 3,671 sessions 2012-2026 the March sub-series alone gives p=0.205, which does NOT reproduce the p=0.041 the sibling got by pooling all four editions. Nothing here licenses an entry.
